newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end up but gains trimmed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end up but gains trimmed.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed higher, bolstered by Friday's USDA quarterly hog report but gains were pared late in the session by profit taking and cash market concerns, traders said.

Early demand from the report lifted October hogs to a new high of 58.350 cents a lb and December 58.050 cents with December briefly limit up before slipping. February lean was up as much as 1.700 cent of the lean contract's 2.000-cent limit.
Hogs ended 1.450 to 0.175 cent higher, paced by February at 77.525 cent, while October settled up 0.375 at 57.725 cents. December finished 0.750 higher at 57.300 cents.
Pork bellies were up near limit of 1.975 cents in February during the day but drifted back to close 0.625 to 0.400 cent higher with February up 0.550 at 78.125 cents.

USDA reported U.S. hog numbers as of September 1 at 58.2 million head, four percent under last year's level. The report showed that expansion of the hog herd was slow in developing despite declining grain prices this quarter.
"Everyone's figuring the near-term (hog) supplies will be tighter" and that took futures higher, said John Nalivka, President of Sterling Marketing Inc.
But price eased as profit taking developed and cash ideas started to weigh on the market, especially October hogs and pork belly futures in general, traders said.
"You have a (pork) cutout that supports maybe a $55 or $56 hog -- but cutout can't sustain $58 hogs," Nalivka said.

Analysts also noted that the peak season for hog marketings is ahead which will weigh on both live market prices and pork product values. This concern over rising pork supplies pared much of the advance in pork bellies, traders said. They said the cash market appears to be topping and increased belly offerings.
"By the end of the week (belly) prices will be $5 to $10 lower," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
"The bacon market is still driven by retail sales and you get those bacon prices too high and will do just what we did in August, take a pretty hard dive," Nalivka added.

In hog options, volatility was unchanged. There was evening up in October which saw buying of 57 and 58 calls and puts. Puts were being offered in February after the sharp rally in futures, pit sources said.
